lexingCheck: Token streams are hand-derived; check_vectors.py re-verifies lexical invariants and harness/crosscheck.py compares them with go/scanner, proc-macro2 and rustc.

vectors.description: Empty input: zero tokens, no k-grams.
Four tokens is fewer than k=5.
Exactly k=5 tokens: one k-gram, partial window selects it.
NFC Unicode identifiers, multi-byte string and char literals; spans are UTF-8 byte offsets.
vectors.inputText:
let größe: &str = "naïve ☃ 世界";
let λ = 'é';

vectors.description: Integer/float forms with suffixes, '2.' float, tuple-index float, raw/byte/raw-byte/C strings.
Lifetimes versus char literals, 'static kept under normalization, raw identifier, single-character punctuation for '->'.
vectors.inputText: fn r#match<'a>(x: &'a str, y: &'static str) -> char { 'a' }

vectors.description: A first line starting '#!' not followed by '[' is a shebang and is skipped.
'#!' followed by '[' is an inner attribute, not a shebang.
Doc comments are dropped like other comments (rustc treats them as doc attributes).
Ten identical tokens: all k-grams identical, every window ties, rightmost minimum wins.
Period-3 token sequence: every window of 4 contains a repeated k-gram, so ties on the minimum are guaranteed.
Reference for the comment/whitespace pair.
Same tokens as rust-format-a with line and nested block comments and different whitespace; fingerprint hashes must be identical.
Reference for the rename pair.
vectors.inputText: fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 { a + b }

vectors.description: Identifiers renamed: exact hashes differ, normalized hashes equal rust-rename-a.
vectors.inputText: fn sum(x: i32, y: i32) -> i32 { x + y }

vectors.description: Byte 0xFF inside a string literal: invalid UTF-8.
Leading byte order mark: rejected (stricter than the Reference, which removes it).
NUL inside a string literal: rejected (stricter than the Reference).
CR not followed by LF: rejected (stricter than the Reference, which treats it as whitespace here).
Nested block comment: the inner '*/' closes only the inner level.
vectors.inputText: fn f() {} /* outer /* inner */ still open

vectors.description: String literal never closed.
Closing '}' while '(' is open.
'ab' is neither a char literal nor a lifetime.
Identifier immediately followed by '"' is a reserved prefix in edition 2021+.
Identifier 'e' + U+0301 is valid XID but not NFC: rejected rather than normalized.
XID boundary code points accepted by Rust: U+2160 (XID_Start), U+00B7 and U+0345 (XID_Continue); all NFC.
U+2E2F VERTICAL TILDE is Pattern_Syntax, not XID: illegal character after the identifier 'a' (Go accepts it as Lm).
U+200D is XID_Continue in Unicode 17.0 but forbidden in identifiers by [ident.zero-width-chars].
Literal suffix 'u8' + 'e' + U+0301 is not NFC; offset is the literal start.
Raw identifier r#e + U+0301 is not NFC; offset is the token start (the 'r').
Non-NFC identifier immediately followed by '"': the NFC check precedes the reserved-prefix check.
'_' after a string with no XID_Continue after it: the Reference SUFFIX cut makes this an error, not a string plus '_'.
Same suffix cut after a char literal.
Suffixes are part of literal tokens: '_' followed by XID_Continue is a valid suffix; 0x1f32 is a hex int; 1e3f32 a float.
Raw lifetimes (edition 2021+) are single lifetime tokens; normalized to empty like other lifetimes.
'r#_ is RESERVED_RAW_LIFETIME.
'##' is RESERVED_POUNDS in edition 2024.
C string with byte, Unicode and ASCII escapes.
C strings forbid the \0 escape.
A raw string with 256 '#' exceeds the 255 limit.
Isolated CR inside a string literal: rejected by the forbidden-code-point scan.
U+FEFF inside a string literal (not at offset 0) is rejected.
Shebang look-ahead: an unterminated block comment counts as comment, so '#!' starts a shebang (matches rustc).
Q1: a raw string ends at the first '"' followed by n '#'; the extra '#' is punctuation.
Q1: after the raw string, '##' is RESERVED_POUNDS.
Q2: errors in scan order; the unterminated string comes before the end-of-input delimiter check.
Q2: scan order: illegal character before the unclosed '('.
Q2: two unclosed openers at end of input: the innermost '[' is reported.
Q3: char and byte literals have no unterminated state: b'a at end of input is malformed.
Q4: C strings accept \x escapes 01-FF.
Q4: \x00 in a C string is malformed.
Q4: any \u{...} spelling of zero (here \u{0_0}) is malformed in a C string.
Q5: a raw lifetime followed by '#' is not reserved: lifetime then '#'.
Q6: lifetime checks run NFC, then zero-width, then the '#' reservation.
Q6: zero-width check precedes the '#' reservation.
Q7: termination is decided first (escape-aware): '"\q' has no closing quote.
Q7: closed literal with an unknown escape is malformed.
Q7: an unterminated raw byte string is unterminated even though its content is not ASCII.
Q8: in the shebang look-ahead '///' is a doc comment, i.e. content, so line 1 is a shebang (Reference SHEBANG, rustc).
Q8: '//!' is a doc comment: shebang.
Q8: '/** d */' is a doc comment: shebang through end of input (no LF), zero tokens.
Q8: '/*! d */' is a doc comment: shebang, zero tokens.
Q8: '////x' is an ordinary comment, so the look-ahead reaches '[': not a shebang.
Q8: '/**/' is an ordinary comment: not a shebang.
Q8: '/***/' is an ordinary comment: not a shebang.
Q8b: U+0085 is white space in the look-ahead: '[' follows, not a shebang.
Q8b: a bare '#!' is a shebang: zero tokens.
Q9: U+0378 is not XID_Continue: illegal character after 'x'. The assigned table is informative only.
Q11: the shebang covers line 1 only, even when a block comment opened on it closes later.
